items.followUp: Explain why the density of air generally decreases as altitude increases.

rubric.why: Identifies how atmospheric pressure changes with altitude.
rubric.description: States that atmospheric pressure decreases as altitude increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of change.

rubric.why: Explains the cause of the pressure change.
rubric.description: Explains that less air lies above a higher location, so the air column weighs less and exerts less pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the smaller amount or weight of air above to lower pressure.

modelAnswer: Atmospheric pressure decreases as we go higher above the Earth.
At higher altitudes, there is a shorter column of air above us, so its weight and the pressure it exerts are smaller.

items.followUp: What is meant by two bodies being in thermal equilibrium?

rubric.why: Identifies the temperature condition for thermal equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the bodies have the same temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating equal temperatures.

rubric.why: Identifies what happens to heat transfer in equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that there is no net flow of heat between the bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no net heat is transferred between them.

modelAnswer: Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium when they are at the same temperature.
There is no net flow of heat between them.

items.followUp: Define temperature and state what happens when two objects at different temperatures are placed in contact.

rubric.why: Defines heat as energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.description: Defines heat as energy transferred from one body to another due to a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the transfer-of-energy definition linked to temperature difference.

rubric.why: Defines internal energy as the energy of the particles in a body.
rubric.description: Defines internal energy as the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of the particles of a substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both kinetic and potential energy of the particles.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from one body to another because of a difference in temperature.
Internal energy is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of the particles of a substance.

items.followUp: Write four differences between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Assesses the difference in the types of quantities.
rubric.description: Mass is a scalar quantity, whereas weight is a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting scalar and vector.

rubric.why: Assesses the meanings of mass and weight.
rubric.description: Mass is the amount of matter in a body; weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing the definitions.

rubric.why: Assesses how mass behaves at different places.
rubric.description: Mass remains constant from place to place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mass does not depend on location.

rubric.why: Assesses how weight behaves at different places.
rubric.description: Weight depends on gravitational acceleration and can vary from place to place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that weight varies with gravity or location.

modelAnswer: Mass is a scalar quantity, whereas weight is a vector quantity.
Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
Mass remains constant from place to place.
Weight depends on gravitational acceleration and may vary from place to place.

items.followUp: A car has an initial velocity of 8 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 4 s. Find its final velocity.

rubric.why: Assesses correct identification of the given quantities.
rubric.description: Identifies initial velocity, acceleration and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given values with units.

rubric.why: Assesses selection of the uniform-acceleration equation.
rubric.description: Writes the relation v = u + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Assesses correct substitution into the formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given values into v = u + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: Assesses the arithmetic result.
rubric.description: Calculates the final velocity as 20.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical result.

rubric.why: Assesses the final answer and SI unit.
rubric.description: Gives the final velocity as 20 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 10 m s⁻¹, a = 2 m s⁻², t = 5 s
Substitution: v = 10 m s⁻¹ + (2 m s⁻²)(5 s)
Answer: The velocity after 5 s is 20 m s⁻¹.

items.followUp: A force makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal. If its horizontal component is 15 N, find the force.

rubric.why: Assesses identification of the horizontal component and angle.
rubric.description: Identifies the horizontal component as 20 N and the angle as 30°.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the given values.

rubric.why: Assesses the component relation.
rubric.description: Uses horizontal component = F cos θ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation.

rubric.why: Assesses rearrangement to find the force.
rubric.description: Rearranges the relation to F = 20/cos 30°.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct rearrangement.

rubric.why: Assesses numerical substitution and calculation.
rubric.description: Evaluates the force as approximately 23.1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical result.

rubric.why: Assesses the final answer with unit.
rubric.description: Gives the force as approximately 23.1 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly rounded answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: horizontal component Fₓ = 20 N, angle θ = 30°

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts over a contact area of 2.0 cm². Calculate the pressure in pascals.

rubric.why: Assesses identification of force and area.
rubric.description: Identifies the force as 75 N and the contact area as 1.5 cm².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given values.

rubric.why: Assesses the pressure formula.
rubric.description: Writes pressure = force/area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Assesses conversion of area to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts 1.5 cm² to 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area conversion.

rubric.why: Assesses substitution using SI units.
rubric.description: Substitutes force and converted area into P = F/A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: Assesses the final pressure and unit.
rubric.description: Calculates the pressure as 5.0 × 10⁵ Pa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

items.followUp: Write the SI units and symbols for time, amount of substance, luminous intensity and thermodynamic temperature.

rubric.why: Assesses the SI units and symbols for length and mass.
rubric.description: Gives metre (m) for length and kilogram (kg) for mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct unit-symbol pairs.

rubric.why: Assesses the SI units and symbols for temperature and electric current.
rubric.description: Gives kelvin (K) for temperature and ampere (A) for electric current.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct unit-symbol pairs.
